raw_response:
I am 65 years old and have farmed these 8 mu in Quzhou County for 40 years. I know every inch of this land, and at my age I do not chase after new fads. My son and his wife work in a factory in Handan, but they come back for harvest. With five mouths to feed, I need a system that is reliable.

The wheat-maize double crop is the backbone of my farm. I will put 6 mu into that rotation. The winter wheat is already in the ground from last autumn. I will use an improved wheat variety—I have seen over four decades that they resist lodging better and give more stable grain than the old traditional seeds. I will apply base fertilizer with compound fertilizer and top-dress urea at the jointing stage in spring. I do not overdo nitrogen because I have learned that too much makes the wheat fall over. Three irrigations from my well—overwinter, jointing, and grain filling—should be enough. I will spray twice for aphids and powdery mildew if they appear. Before sowing I always do rotary tillage to get a fine seedbed. I expect about 460 kg per mu.

For summer maize, timing is everything. As soon as the wheat comes off in early June, I will plant a hybrid like Zhengdan 958. There is no time for deep ploughing, so I will do no-tillage or very light rotary into the wheat stubble to catch the season and keep soil moisture. Maize needs nitrogen, but less fuss than wheat—base dressing plus one top-dressing. Two irrigations at the critical stages, and two pesticide sprays for corn borers and leaf blight. If the weather cooperates, 500 kg per mu is a honest expectation.

The remaining 2 mu I will plant to Bt cotton hybrid. My wife helps with the autumn picking. Cotton needs patience and more potassium for the bolls. I will rotary till in spring, plant in late April or early May, and irrigate three times during flowering and boll setting. Even with Bt seed, I still need three pesticide applications for aphids and spider mites. I expect around 260 kg of seed cotton per mu.

This is what I will do because it has fed my family for 40 years, and I trust what works.
